rows.text: Read Yasharn's second line slowly, because it is much wider than it looks. "Players can't pay life or sacrifice nonland permanents to cast spells or activate abilities" turns off Treasures, Clues, Food, every sacrifice outlet, every Phyrexian mana symbol, Force of Will's alternative cost, Necropotence, Bolas's Citadel and Mana Confluence — for the whole table, at once. This deck is built so that none of that costs you anything, and then it stacks the rest of the lock on top.

rows.name: Yasharn, Implacable Earth
rows.text: fetches a basic Forest AND a basic Plains to your hand on arrival, which fuels the extra land drops below, and then shuts off an enormous slice of the format. Four mana, a 4/4 body, and against an aristocrats or storm table it is close to a hard lock on its own.
Note what it does NOT stop: fetchlands sacrifice a LAND, so those still work. It is nonland permanents only.
Note also that it is symmetrical. This deck runs no Treasures, no sacrifice outlets and no pay-life costs precisely so that the symmetry is free.

rows.name: Archon of Emeria
rows.text: one spell per turn each, and their nonbasics arrive tapped.

rows.name: Rule of Law
rows.text: the enchantment copy, which removal reaches less easily.

rows.name: Gaddock Teeg
rows.text: no noncreature spell of mana value four or more, and no noncreature X spells at all. That is most wraths and most finishers.

rows.name: Drannith Magistrate
rows.text: no casting from graveyards, exile or the command zone. It turns off every other commander at the table.

rows.name: Linvala, Keeper of Silence
rows.text: their creatures' activated abilities all stop.

rows.name: Collector Ouphe
rows.text: every artifact activated ability stops, theirs and yours.

rows.name: Cursed Totem
rows.text: the creature version. Careful — it blanks Kamahl's land animation too.

rows.name: Containment Priest
rows.text: anything entering without being cast is exiled. It blanks reanimation and blink outright.

rows.name: Root Maze
rows.text: their artifacts and lands enter tapped, which quietly costs a ramp deck a turn every turn.

rows.name: Grand Abolisher
rows.text: they cannot act at all during your turn.

rows.name: Aven Mindcensor
rows.text: flash him onto a fetchland or a tutor.

rows.name: Archon of Valor's Reach
rows.text: name a card type and NOBODY can cast it. Against a spell deck name instant; against artifacts, artifact. Your own deck is creatures, lands and a handful of enchantments, so the cost to you is usually nothing.

rows.name: Rest in Peace
rows.text: no graveyards, and this deck never uses its own.

rows.name: Blind Obedience
rows.text: their creatures and artifacts enter tapped, and extort drains on every spell you cast.

rows.name: Hushbringer
rows.text: creatures entering or dying trigger nothing. That is devastating against half the format — and it also blanks your own Aura Shards, Elesh Norn, Mother of Machines, and Yasharn's land fetch. Play it when the table is built on enter-the-battlefield value and you are not, and be deliberate about the order: get your own triggers first, then land it.

rows.name: Dryad of the Ilysian Grove
rows.text: an extra land drop, and your lands become every basic type — which turns Farseek and Nature's Lore into "fetch any land you own".

rows.name: Exploration
rows.text: the cheapest extra land drop.

rows.name: Oracle of Mul Daya
rows.text: an extra drop plus lands off the top of your library.

rows.name: Karametra, God of Harvests
rows.text: a land for every creature spell you cast, and an indestructible body once devotion gets there. In a deck of hatebears that is a land a turn.

rows.name: Nature's Lore
rows.text: an untapped dual with a basic type.

rows.name: Farseek
rows.text: the same for shocklands.

rows.name: Cultivate
rows.text: a land down and a land in hand.

rows.name: Kodama's Reach
rows.text: the second copy.

rows.name: Rampant Growth
rows.text: the cheap one.

rows.name: Fertile Ground
rows.text: an extra mana of any colour off a land.

guide.title: Removal that works under your own lock

rows.name: Get Lost
rows.text: creature, enchantment or planeswalker, for two mana, at instant speed.

rows.name: Generous Gift
rows.text: any permanent at all.

rows.name: Grasp of Fate
rows.text: exiles a nonland permanent from EVERY opponent, on one card.

rows.name: Darksteel Mutation
rows.text: turns a commander into a 0/1 Insect it cannot recast.

rows.name: Krosan Grip
rows.text: split second, so it beats the response.

rows.name: Nature's Claim
rows.text: one mana for any artifact or enchantment; the four life they gain is irrelevant.

rows.name: Manglehorn
rows.text: an artifact on entry, and theirs enter tapped.

rows.name: Aura Shards
rows.text: with a board of hatebears, every creature you play destroys an artifact or enchantment. It is how this deck beats a stax mirror.

rows.name: Final Showdown
rows.text: spree, so you choose. Strip all abilities and wrath in one cast, and give one of your own creatures indestructible on the way — a wrath that beats indestructible and hatebears alike.

rows.name: Heroic Intervention
rows.text: hexproof and indestructible for everything through their wrath.

rows.name: Esper Sentinel
rows.text: taxes their first noncreature spell each turn.

rows.name: Archivist of Oghma
rows.text: a card and a life every time anyone searches — and Aven Mindcensor makes searching worse for them at the same time.

rows.name: Eladamri's Call
rows.text: instant-speed tutor for whichever hate bear the table is weak to.

rows.name: Enlightened Tutor
rows.text: finds Rule of Law, Grasp of Fate, Aura Shards or Rest in Peace.

rows.name: Ohran Frostfang
rows.text: deathtouch on every attacker and a card for each one that connects. It turns a stalled board into a clock.

rows.name: Kamahl, Heart of Krosa
rows.text: +3/+3 and trample to the team every combat, and he animates lands so the attack is wider than it looks. This is the deck's main finisher.

rows.name: Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite
rows.text: +2/+2 to yours and -2/-2 to theirs. Against a token or hatebear table it is a one-sided wrath that stays on the battlefield.

rows.name: Ohran Frostfang
rows.text: nobody can block profitably, and every hit refuels your hand.

rows.name: Archon of Valor's Reach
rows.text: a 5/6 flying vigilant trampler is a real clock while the lock holds.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep ramp and a cheap hate piece. Turn-one Exploration or a turn-two Rampant Growth into a turn-three Archon of Emeria or Gaddock Teeg is the start that wins games; a hand of five-drops is not.

Read the pod before choosing what to deploy. Yasharn against aristocrats and storm, Containment Priest against reanimator, Drannith Magistrate against a commander-centric table, Archon of Valor's Reach naming instant against a blue one.

rows.name: Yasharn, Implacable Earth
rows.text: cast him even when the lock line is not obviously relevant. The two basics he fetches feed the extra land drops, and a 4/4 blocks most of what the format attacks with.

Watch your own lock. Cursed Totem stops Kamahl activating, Collector Ouphe stops your own mana rocks if you ever add any, and Hushbringer stops Aura Shards. None of those is a reason not to play them — it is a reason to sequence them last.
